sentences.text: Researchers tested eight different CXCL9 protein versions and peptides to separate the N-terminal core from the C-terminal tail, finding that CXCL9 encourages nerve fiber growth and cell survival in PC12 cells and sympathetic neurons without needing the CXCR3 receptor.

Protein versions missing the C-terminal tail showed no ability to support nerve growth or activate the ERK1/2 and Akt signaling pathways, whereas the C-terminal tail alone was enough to restore nerve growth, cell survival, and neuron rescue regardless of the protein carrier used.
The authors conclude that the neurotrophic effects of CXCL9 come specifically from its basic C-terminal tail and not from its standard N-terminal domain.
